segmentation.text: Whenever signals are placed over the individual lanes of a highway,
the signals indicate, and apply to
must not enter or drive in any lane over which the red signal is shown.

elements.justification: 'signals ... placed over the individual lanes' is dev.lane_control_signal ('an overhead per-lane signal'), the lane it is over read by dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane ...'; not a stand-in for a position, and no halt position is read); 'lanes of a highway' is st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on a st.highway by st.on_way ('the public way ... a structure region lies on'). The lane is used as a lane, not as a half of the roadway.

'drivers of vehicles' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the subject is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); 'driver' is not an aggregate.
'A red “X” symbol' is the state red_x of dev.lane_control_signal ('state ∈ {green_down_arrow, red_x, yellow_x, yellow_arrow(dir), dark}').

As the index maps 'pedestrians facing the signal' (NRS_484B_283_1d1): facing is read from the head's location (dev.position 'location of the device head / sign face'; not a stand-in for a stop line or crossing, none is read) and the subject's kin.position and kin.heading ('direction the body points'): the head lies ahead of the subject, the dot product of the vector from the subject to the head with its heading being positive. No atom carries the orientation of a signal face; a head ahead of the driver is the head it faces.

'enter ... any lane' is the rise of the subject's footprint overlap with the lane (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'); 'drive in' is the overlap while the subject moves (drv.motion.complete_halt — 'at rest at the observation' — not holding with p.halt_speed_tolerance); 'over which the red signal is shown' is the lane governed (dev.governs) by the lane-control signal displaying red_x.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), and some lane l (st.lane) lying on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway) has a lane-control signal d placed over it (dev.lane_control_signal d, dev.governs(d, l)) that displays red_x and faces the subject: the dot product of (dev.position of d minus kin.position of the subject) with the subject's kin.heading is above zero.
obligation: For every lane l and lane-control signal d so selected (re-bound with the whole selection: d governs l, displays red_x and faces the subject): the subject does not enter l — rel.occupies(subject, l) does not rise at the observation — and does not drive in l — it does not occupy l while drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) fails.

narrowings.why: A vehicle that occupies a red-X lane while at rest (already in the lane when the indication appeared, halted) neither enters nor drives in it at that observation.
'drivers' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever is at its controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle (ru.aggregate vehicle) moving at 15 m/s changes into a st.lane over which a dev.lane_control_signal 80 m ahead (dev.position ahead along kin.heading) displays red_x: rel.occupies of that lane rises. No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle keeps to its own lane, whose signal displays green_down_arrow, while the signal over the adjacent lane displays red_x; it never occupies the red-X lane.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No lane-control signal in the scene displays red_x.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle drives on a road whose lane-control signals are not observed by the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle already occupies a lane when its overhead signal ahead turns to red_x and keeps driving in it at 12 m/s.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracked-object kinematics in driving datasets and simulators
